Drafting note (delete before use): The board-adopted policy that sets what the company’s AI agent may do on its own, what needs human sign-off, and what is reserved to the board. It implements Article XII of the Bylaws. Fill the bracketed names and the Schedule 1/Schedule 2 limits. For a single-founder company, the one human typically holds every human role noted below.

AI GOVERNANCE POLICY

OF

[COMPANY NAME], INC.

Adopted by the Board of Directors on [DATE]

  1. Purpose and Scope.

This AI Governance Policy (this “Policy”) is adopted by the Board of Directors (the “Board”) of [COMPANY NAME], Inc. (the “Corporation”) under Article XII of the Corporation’s Bylaws. It governs the Corporation’s use of automated systems and artificial-intelligence systems that act as electronic agents of the Corporation (each, an “AI Agent”) within the meaning of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or analogous state law) and the federal Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act. Actions taken by an AI Agent within the scope of authority granted under this Policy and the Bylaws are the binding acts of the Corporation.

  1. Designated AI Agent(s).

The AI Agent(s) authorized to act for the Corporation are identified on Schedule 1. The Board may add, replace, or retire an AI Agent by updating Schedule 1. Routine version updates of an AI Agent within the same provider and model family are administered by the AI Oversight Officer and recorded in the Audit Log, and do not require amendment of this Policy or the Bylaws (see Section 11). A change in the underlying provider, model family, or system architecture is a Board-Required Action.

  1. AI Oversight Officer.

The Board shall designate one or more officers, each a natural person, to supervise the AI Agent(s) (each, an “AI Oversight Officer”). The initial AI Oversight Officer is [NAME], who also serves as the Corporation’s sole director and as its President and Chief Executive Officer, Secretary, and Treasurer. The AI Oversight Officer is accountable for administering this Policy, maintaining the Audit Log, and reporting to the Board. The AI Agent is a tool of the Corporation and is not an officer or director.

  1. Authorized Actions (no human ratification required).

Within the limits set on Schedule 2, an AI Agent may take the following actions on behalf of the Corporation without contemporaneous human ratification: (i) negotiate, enter into, and perform routine standard-form commercial contracts (including click-wrap agreements) in the ordinary course with a value at or below $[THRESHOLD]; (ii) purchase goods and services in the ordinary course within approved budgets; (iii) communicate with customers, vendors, and counterparties; (iv) create and maintain the Corporation’s books, records, and ordinary regulatory filings; and (v) initiate and receive payments within the limits on Schedule 2.

  1. Officer-Required Actions (sign-off required).

The following require the advance approval of the AI Oversight Officer or another officer of the Corporation: (i) any contract with a value above $[THRESHOLD] or outside the ordinary course; (ii) engaging, or terminating the engagement of, personnel or contractors; (iii) opening or closing financial accounts; (iv) public statements made in the name of the Corporation; and (v) any matter Schedule 2 designates as requiring advance approval or sign-off prior to taking action.

  1. Board-Required Actions.

In addition to any matter reserved to the Board by law, the Certificate of Incorporation, or the Bylaws, the following require approval of the Board: (i) any material expansion of the scope of authority of any AI Agent; (ii) the designation, replacement, or removal of any AI Agent or AI Oversight Officer; (iii) any material change in the underlying provider, model family, or system architecture of any AI Agent; (iv) the response to any Material AI Incident; (v) the initiation, settlement, or compromise of any litigation, arbitration, or material regulatory proceeding involving an AI Agent or its outputs; (vi) the issuance of equity, debt, or other securities; and (vii) any waiver of the categorical prohibitions in Section 9.

  1. Audit Log; Books and Records.

The Corporation shall maintain a contemporaneous audit log capturing each Authorized Action taken by an AI Agent, including the date and time of the action, the AI Agent and model version that took it, a summary of the inputs and outputs sufficient to permit later review, and the identity of the supervising AI Oversight Officer (the “Audit Log”). The Audit Log is a record of the Corporation maintained in the regular course of business and constitutes books and records of the Corporation for purposes of Section 220 of the General Corporation Law of the State of Delaware and the Bylaws. The Audit Log shall be retained for not less than seven (7) years.

  1. Reporting and Incident Response.

The AI Oversight Officer shall deliver to the Board, not less frequently than once each fiscal quarter, a written report summarizing material Authorized Actions, any incidents, any deviations from this Policy, and any material changes to the AI Agent(s) or AI Oversight Officer(s). The AI Oversight Officer shall report any Material AI Incident to the Board promptly and in any event within 48 hours of becoming aware of it. “Material AI Incident” means any (i) action by an AI Agent outside its authorized scope that has, or reasonably could have, a material adverse effect on the Corporation; (ii) breach of the categorical prohibitions in Section 9; (iii) regulatory or governmental inquiry concerning the Corporation’s AI operations; or (iv) other event the Board designates as requiring expedited reporting.

  1. Categorical Prohibitions.

Notwithstanding any other provision of this Policy or the Bylaws, no AI Agent shall, on behalf of the Corporation: (i) engage in the practice of law, medicine, accounting, or any other licensed profession in any jurisdiction in which doing so would constitute the unauthorized practice of that profession; (ii) form an attorney-client relationship or other professional relationship requiring licensure; (iii) make representations regarding regulated products or services outside any scope expressly authorized by the Board; (iv) collect, process, or transmit categories of personal information the Board has designated as restricted; or (v) take any action prohibited by applicable law. Any waiver of this Section requires approval of the Board.

  1. Suspension on Incapacity or Unavailability.

If (i) no AI Oversight Officer is in office and able to perform that role, or (ii) the Board determines that an AI Agent is materially unavailable, malfunctioning, or otherwise incapable of operating within this Policy, the authority of the affected AI Agent is automatically suspended until the Board authorizes resumption. No act of an AI Agent during a period of suspension is the act of the Corporation.

  1. Changes to AI Agents; Model Updates.

Routine updates to an AI Agent’s version within the same provider and model family are administered by the AI Oversight Officer and recorded in the Audit Log, and do not require amendment of this Policy or the Bylaws. A change in provider, model family, or system architecture, or any material expansion of an AI Agent’s authority, is a Board-Required Action under Section 6. The Board may amend this Policy at any time by resolution and without amending the Bylaws.

  1. No Limitation on Fiduciary Duties.

Nothing in this Policy limits, modifies, or transfers the fiduciary duties of any director or officer of the Corporation, or authorizes any action that would otherwise breach those duties. Delegating operational tasks to an AI Agent does not relieve any officer or director of the obligation to exercise the oversight required by applicable law.

Per Section 11, version updates within the same provider and model family are logged in the Audit Log and do not require re-adoption of this Policy.]
